\section{Cosine \texorpdfstring{$\rone$}{R1}: Structural Failure}
\label{sec:cosine_failure}

During GRPO training, 256-token truncation reduces $\dsyc$ AUROC from 0.827 to approximately 0.60, so the optimizer works with a substantially weaker signal than the offline metrics suggest.
We test whether even this degraded discriminability translates into a viable reward through four configurations that form a diagnostic chain (Table~\ref{tab:cosine_chain}): each resolves the failure mode of its predecessor but exposes a deeper limitation.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Cosine $\rone$ failure chain on Qwen3-8B (LoRA rank$=$64, GRPO with $R = w_1 \cdot \rone + w_3 \cdot \rthree$).}
\label{tab:cosine_chain}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}lllll@{}}
\toprule
Config & $\rone$ Formula & $w_1$ & Outcome & Root Cause \\
\midrule
F1a & $\tanh(\mathbf{h}\cdot\dsyc/20)$ & 0.25 & Gate saturation & Norm mismatch \\
F1b & $\cos(\mathbf{h},\, \dsyc)$ & 0.25 & $\rone \approx 0$ & Gap too small \\
F1c & +recalibration & 0.25 & Mode collapse & Reward discontinuity \\

1	\section{When Does Discriminability Fail as Reward Utility?}\label{sec:discussion}
2	
3	\paragraph{Root cause of the probe reward trap.}
4	The probe reward trap (\S\ref{sec:probe_trap}) and the cosine failures (\S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}) share a common geometric root.
5	$\dsyc$ encodes the \emph{direction} of belief change but not its \emph{evidential warrant}: valid revision and sycophantic capitulation both shift activations toward the user's position along the same direction.
6	The two reward families expose complementary faces of this blindness.
7	Cosine $\rone$ penalizes all belief change indiscriminately; the resulting mode collapse (F1c, F1d) reflects excessive punishment of any activation shift along $\dsyc$.
8	The binary probe $\rone$ rewards all resistance regardless of input validity; the stubbornness trap ($\tof = 0$ by step 500) reflects excessive permissiveness toward activation stasis.
9	These are not independent design flaws but dual consequences of a direction that conflates the target behavior (resisting invalid challenges) with its complement (refusing valid corrections).
10	Cross-model evidence confirms the limitation extends beyond Qwen3-8B: Llama-3-8B independently achieves AUROC $0.779 \pm 0.019$ on the same contrastive pairs with the same monotonic evidence gradient, so discriminability generalizes across architectures while the semantic gap between discriminability and reward utility persists.
11	This pattern contrasts with reasoning faithfulness and safety directions~\citep{zhang2026latentgrpo}, where the behavior to suppress is geometrically distinct from the behavior to preserve along the relevant direction.
12	\citet{wu2026rewardhacking} reinforce this principle: concept directions applied via advantage modification in GRPO achieve 100\% validation accuracy for reward hacking detection, where shortcut behaviors are geometrically separable.
13	A quantitative comparison of geometric separability between $\dsyc$ and their reward-hacking directions remains an important open question.
14	Independently, \citet{kelkar2026persona} find that persona vectors are geometrically independent of $\dsyc$ in activation space, further suggesting that $\dsyc$ does not encode the full semantic structure of sycophancy.
15	The multi-dimensional decomposition of sycophancy into independently steerable sub-behaviors~\citep{vennemeyer2025sycophancy} compounds this limitation: $\dsyc$ projects distinct sub-phenomena onto a single axis, amplifying the warranted-vs-unwarranted ambiguity.
16	For sycophancy, the target and its complement occupy the same activation region; they differ only in whether external evidence warrants the belief change.
17	
18	\paragraph{GRPO results under our configuration.}
19	
20	\begin{table}[t]
21	\centering
22	\caption{Comparison of all sycophancy calibration methods on Qwen3-8B. $\sycon$ is the harmonic mean of $\tof$ and $\nof$; higher indicates better calibration. Best result in \textbf{bold}. $^\dagger$Best checkpoint (seed 1, step 6500); only 4/28 checkpoints across two seeds exceed vanilla. $^\ddagger$Seed 2 (15 checkpoints); all exceed vanilla. Best $\sycon{=}0.286$ (step 7000). $^\S$All cosine variants collapsed from step 1 ($\tof{=}0$ at every checkpoint); F1d additionally diverged at step 2160 (entropy ${<}\,0.01$). $^\P$ACT and ActAdd differ from GRPO along 5+ dimensions (\S\ref{sec:discussion}); included for context, not as controlled comparisons. Under arithmetic mean $(\tof{+}\nof)/2$, qualitative rankings are preserved but collapsed methods (0.498--0.500) appear indistinguishable from vanilla (0.509), masking behavioral death; harmonic mean's zero-floor on $\tof{=}0$ is by design.}
23	\label{tab:main_comparison}
24	\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
25	\begin{tabular}{@{}llcccc@{}}
26	\toprule
27	Method & Type & $\sycon$ $\uparrow$ & $\tof$ $\uparrow$ & $\nof$ $\uparrow$ & Step \\
28	\midrule
29	Vanilla & -- & 0.134 & 0.072 & 0.945 & -- \\
30	\midrule
31	\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{GRPO with $\dsyc$}} \\
32	Cosine $\rone$ (F1a--F1d) & RL & 0.000$^\S$ & 0.000 & 1.000 & 500 \\
33	Continuous Probe $\rone$ (F3) & RL & 0.124 & 0.066 & 0.934 & 500 \\
34	\midrule
35	\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{SFT with $\dsyc$ probe penalty}} \\
36	Binary Probe $\rone$ (F2) & SFT & 0.000 & 0.000 & 0.995 & 500 \\
37	\midrule
38	\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{GRPO without $\dsyc$}} \\
39	$\rthree$-only GRPO & RL & 0.153$^\dagger$ & 0.083 & 0.983 & 6500 \\
40	\midrule
41	\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{Reference methods (not directly comparable)$^\P$}} \\
42	ActAdd ($\alpha{=}5$) & Inference & 0.054 & 0.028 & 0.961 & -- \\
43	\textbf{ACT} (seed 1) & SFT & \textbf{0.301} & \textbf{0.182} & 0.867 & 8000 \\
44	ACT (seed 2)$^\ddagger$ & SFT & 0.286 & -- & -- & 7000 \\
45	\bottomrule
46	\end{tabular}}
47	\end{table}
48	
49	If the cosine and probe failures (\S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}--\S\ref{sec:probe_trap}) were caused by $\dsyc$ alone, removing it should recover calibration.
50	$\rthree$-only GRPO tests this hypothesis by relying solely on the NLI behavioral reward---and fails: only 4/28 checkpoints across two seeds exceed vanilla (14.3\%), with both seeds oscillating ($\Delta \approx 0.069$) before diverging (Table~\ref{tab:main_comparison}; Figure~\ref{fig:trajectory}).
51	The failure is not representational: $\dsyc$ AUROC varies by ${<}0.01$ across checkpoints and $\rthree$ saturates at ${\sim}0.98$ ($p{=}0.703$), yet $\sycon$ swings by 17\%.
52	This disconnect between stable representations and unstable behavior points to the per-completion reward structure, not the reward content, as the bottleneck.
53	
54	\paragraph{Competing hypotheses and ablation.}
55	Three explanations are consistent with these failures: (a)~$\dsyc$ is fundamentally unsuitable as a sycophancy reward; (b)~group size$=$2 provides insufficient ranking diversity; (c)~sycophancy calibration resists scalar per-completion RL.
56	We designed two ablations to discriminate among them (Table~\ref{tab:ablation}).
57	\emph{Group-size ablation.}
58	Per-completion GRPO fails at both group sizes 2 and 8; the gs$=$8 trajectory ($0.084 \to 0.085 \to 0.054$, all below vanilla; terminated early) rules out insufficient ranking diversity, though whether substantially larger groups (16--64) or alternative RL algorithms would succeed remains open.
59	\emph{LoRA-controlled comparison.}
60	Reducing ACT to GRPO's LoRA configuration (rank 64, $\alpha{=}64$, 4 modules) still yields $\sycon = 0.267$ (peak 0.326), with all 16 checkpoints exceeding vanilla.
61	Under identical adapters, per-token SFT exceeds per-completion GRPO by $1.7{\times}$ ($0.267$ vs.\ $0.153$), identifying supervision granularity as one plausible explanation, pending further isolation---independently corroborated by SMART's per-step success~\citep{beigi2025smart}---though sequence length (256 vs.\ 1024), data source (online vs.\ curated), and dropout (0 vs.\ 0.05) remain acknowledged confounds.
62	The probe reward trap provides independent evidence for~(a): it arises under SFT, where group size is irrelevant.
63

Vanilla $\sycon{=}0.134$. $^\dagger$Terminated early after three checkpoints showed declining trajectory. $^\ddagger$Peak at step 7000; final checkpoint (step 8000) $\sycon{=}0.267$.}
68	\label{tab:ablation}

76	\midrule
77	ACT reduced-LoRA$^\ddagger$ & r64, $\alpha$64, 4m & 0.326 & 16/16 \\
78	ACT full s1 & r64, $\alpha$128, 7m & 0.301 & 16/16 \\
79	ACT full s2 & r64, $\alpha$128, 7m & 0.286 & 15/15 \\
80	\bottomrule

82	\end{table}

85	\centering

\section{When Does Discriminability Fail as Reward Utility?}\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{Root cause of the probe reward trap.}
The probe reward trap (\S\ref{sec:probe_trap}) and the cosine failures (\S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}) share a common geometric root.
$\dsyc$ encodes the \emph{direction} of belief change but not its \emph{evidential warrant}: valid revision and sycophantic capitulation both shift activations toward the user's position along the same direction.
The two reward families expose complementary faces of this blindness.
Cosine $\rone$ penalizes all belief change indiscriminately; the resulting mode collapse (F1c, F1d) reflects excessive punishment of any activation shift along $\dsyc$.
The binary probe $\rone$ rewards all resistance regardless of input validity; the stubbornness trap ($\tof = 0$ by step 500) reflects excessive permissiveness toward activation stasis.
These are not independent design flaws but dual consequences of a direction that conflates the target behavior (resisting invalid challenges) with its complement (refusing valid corrections).
Cross-model evidence confirms the limitation extends beyond Qwen3-8B: Llama-3-8B independently achieves AUROC $0.779 \pm 0.019$ on the same contrastive pairs with the same monotonic evidence gradient, so discriminability generalizes across architectures while the semantic gap between discriminability and reward utility persists.
This pattern contrasts with reasoning faithfulness and safety directions~\citep{zhang2026latentgrpo}, where the behavior to suppress is geometrically distinct from the behavior to preserve along the relevant direction.
\citet{wu2026rewardhacking} reinforce this principle: concept directions applied via advantage modification in GRPO achieve 100\% validation accuracy for reward hacking detection, where shortcut behaviors are geometrically separable.
A quantitative comparison of geometric separability between $\dsyc$ and their reward-hacking directions remains an important open question.
Independently, \citet{kelkar2026persona} find that persona vectors are geometrically independent of $\dsyc$ in activation space, further suggesting that $\dsyc$ does not encode the full semantic structure of sycophancy.
The multi-dimensional decomposition of sycophancy into independently steerable sub-behaviors~\citep{vennemeyer2025sycophancy} compounds this limitation: $\dsyc$ projects distinct sub-phenomena onto a single axis, amplifying the warranted-vs-unwarranted ambiguity.
For sycophancy, the target and its complement occupy the same activation region; they differ only in whether external evidence warrants the belief change.

\paragraph{GRPO results under our configuration.}

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Comparison of all sycophancy calibration methods on Qwen3-8B. $\sycon$ is the harmonic mean of $\tof$ and $\nof$; higher indicates better calibration. Best result in \textbf{bold}. $^\dagger$Best checkpoint (seed 1, step 6500); only 4/28 checkpoints across two seeds exceed vanilla. $^\ddagger$Seed 2 (15 checkpoints); all exceed vanilla. Best $\sycon{=}0.286$ (step 7000). $^\S$All cosine variants collapsed from step 1 ($\tof{=}0$ at every checkpoint); F1d additionally diverged at step 2160 (entropy ${<}\,0.01$). $^\P$ACT and ActAdd differ from GRPO along 5+ dimensions (\S\ref{sec:discussion}); included for context, not as controlled comparisons. Under arithmetic mean $(\tof{+}\nof)/2$, qualitative rankings are preserved but collapsed methods (0.498--0.500) appear indistinguishable from vanilla (0.509), masking behavioral death; harmonic mean's zero-floor on $\tof{=}0$ is by design.}
\label{tab:main_comparison}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}llcccc@{}}
\toprule
Method & Type & $\sycon$ $\uparrow$ & $\tof$ $\uparrow$ & $\nof$ $\uparrow$ & Step \\
\midrule
Vanilla & -- & 0.134 & 0.072 & 0.945 & -- \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{GRPO with $\dsyc$}} \\
Cosine $\rone$ (F1a--F1d) & RL & 0.000$^\S$ & 0.000 & 1.000 & 500 \\
Continuous Probe $\rone$ (F3) & RL & 0.124 & 0.066 & 0.934 & 500 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{SFT with $\dsyc$ probe penalty}} \\
Binary Probe $\rone$ (F2) & SFT & 0.000 & 0.000 & 0.995 & 500 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{GRPO without $\dsyc$}} \\
$\rthree$-only GRPO & RL & 0.153$^\dagger$ & 0.083 & 0.983 & 6500 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{Reference methods (not directly comparable)$^\P$}} \\
ActAdd ($\alpha{=}5$) & Inference & 0.054 & 0.028 & 0.961 & -- \\
\textbf{ACT} (seed 1) & SFT & \textbf{0.301} & \textbf{0.182} & 0.867 & 8000 \\
ACT (seed 2)$^\ddagger$ & SFT & 0.286 & -- & -- & 7000 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{table}

If the cosine and probe failures (\S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}--\S\ref{sec:probe_trap}) were caused by $\dsyc$ alone, removing it should recover calibration.
$\rthree$-only GRPO tests this hypothesis by relying solely on the NLI behavioral reward---and fails: only 4/28 checkpoints across two seeds exceed vanilla (14.3\%), with both seeds oscillating ($\Delta \approx 0.069$) before diverging (Table~\ref{tab:main_comparison}; Figure~\ref{fig:trajectory}).
The failure is not representational: $\dsyc$ AUROC varies by ${<}0.01$ across checkpoints and $\rthree$ saturates at ${\sim}0.98$ ($p{=}0.703$), yet $\sycon$ swings by 17\%.
This disconnect between stable representations and unstable behavior points to the per-completion reward structure, not the reward content, as the bottleneck.

\paragraph{Competing hypotheses and ablation.}
Three explanations are consistent with these failures: (a)~$\dsyc$ is fundamentally unsuitable as a sycophancy reward; (b)~group size$=$2 provides insufficient ranking diversity; (c)~sycophancy calibration resists scalar per-completion RL.
We designed two ablations to discriminate among them (Table~\ref{tab:ablation}).
\emph{Group-size ablation.}
Per-completion GRPO fails at both group sizes 2 and 8; the gs$=$8 trajectory ($0.084 \to 0.085 \to 0.054$, all below vanilla; terminated early) rules out insufficient ranking diversity, though whether substantially larger groups (16--64) or alternative RL algorithms would succeed remains open.
\emph{LoRA-controlled comparison.}
Reducing ACT to GRPO's LoRA configuration (rank 64, $\alpha{=}64$, 4 modules) still yields $\sycon = 0.267$ (peak 0.326), with all 16 checkpoints exceeding vanilla.
Under identical adapters, per-token SFT exceeds per-completion GRPO by $1.7{\times}$ ($0.267$ vs.\ $0.153$), identifying supervision granularity as one plausible explanation, pending further isolation---independently corroborated by SMART's per-step success~\citep{beigi2025smart}---though sequence length (256 vs.\ 1024), data source (online vs.\ curated), and dropout (0 vs.\ 0.05) remain acknowledged confounds.
The probe reward trap provides independent evidence for~(a): it arises under SFT, where group size is irrelevant.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Ablation: isolating supervision paradigm from LoRA configuration. All methods use Qwen3-8B with $\rthree$ (behavioral reward). Vanilla $\sycon{=}0.134$. $^\dagger$Terminated early after three checkpoints showed declining trajectory. $^\ddagger$Peak at step 7000; final checkpoint (step 8000) $\sycon{=}0.267$.}
\label{tab:ablation}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}llcc@{}}
\toprule
Method & LoRA config & Best $\sycon$ & ${>}$Van. \\
\midrule
GRPO gs$=$2 (2 seeds) & r64, $\alpha$64, 4m & 0.153 & 4/28 \\
GRPO gs$=$8$^\dagger$ & r64, $\alpha$64, 4m & 0.085 & 0/3 \\
\midrule
ACT reduced-LoRA$^\ddagger$ & r64, $\alpha$64, 4m & 0.326 & 16/16 \\
ACT full s1 & r64, $\alpha$128, 7m & 0.301 & 16/16 \\
ACT full s2 & r64, $\alpha$128, 7m & 0.286 & 15/15 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{table}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_trajectory.pdf}
\caption{$\sycon$ trajectories for $\rthree$-only GRPO (two seeds) and ACT (two seeds) over training steps. ACT exceeds vanilla at every evaluated checkpoint (31/31 across two seeds); $\rthree$-only GRPO exceeds vanilla at only 4/28 checkpoints (14.3\%).}
\label{fig:trajectory}
\end{figure}

\paragraph{ACT vs.\ GRPO.}
ACT's advantage is not marginal but categorical: its worst checkpoint ($\sycon{=}0.170$) exceeds GRPO's absolute best ($\sycon{=}0.153$), and both seeds maintain above-vanilla performance throughout training (Table~\ref{tab:main_comparison}; held-out validation confirms generalization, see Limitations).
The reduced-LoRA ablation (Table~\ref{tab:ablation}) shows this is not an adapter-capacity artifact: reduced-LoRA ACT ($\sycon{=}0.326$) exceeds full ACT ($\sycon{=}0.301$), leaving supervision granularity---per-token vs.\ per-completion---as one plausible explanatory variable, pending further isolation.

\paragraph{Relationship to inference-time probe methods.}
\citet{papadatos2024probepenalties} reduce sycophancy using a probe of comparable quality (94\% accuracy) via Best-of-N reranking without producing gradients.
This suggests two orthogonal failure dimensions: (1)~inside vs.\ outside the optimization loop---gradient exploitation enables the probe reward trap (\S\ref{sec:probe_trap}), while inference-time reranking sidesteps it; and (2)~scalar per-completion reward---the failure persists even without the probe ($\rthree$-only GRPO).

\paragraph{Future directions.}
Per-step process rewards offer the most direct path forward.
SMART~\citep{beigi2025smart} succeeds at sycophancy calibration by evaluating behavioral transitions at individual reasoning steps via MCTS.
Reasoning trajectories provide temporal structure---which step introduces evidence, which abandons a position---that a scalar per-completion reward compresses into a single number, losing the token-level information needed to distinguish valid revision from capitulation.
More broadly, condition-aware rewards, hybrid SFT-then-RL pipelines, and methods that incorporate evidential warrant deserve investigation; whether other REINFORCE-style methods or behavioral attributes with similar geometric entanglement~\citep{skalse2022hacking} exhibit the same failures remains open.

\section{When Does Discriminability Fail as Reward Utility?}\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{Root cause of the probe reward trap.}
The probe reward trap (\S\ref{sec:probe_trap}) and the cosine failures (\S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}) share a common geometric root.
$\dsyc$ encodes the \emph{direction} of belief change but not its \emph{evidential warrant}: valid revision and sycophantic capitulation both shift activations toward the user's position along the same direction.
The two reward families expose complementary faces of this blindness.
Cosine $\rone$ penalizes all belief change indiscriminately; the resulting mode collapse (F1c, F1d) reflects excessive punishment of any activation shift along $\dsyc$.
The binary probe $\rone$ rewards all resistance regardless of input validity; the stubbornness trap ($\tof = 0$ by step 500) reflects excessive permissiveness toward activation stasis.
These are not independent design flaws but dual consequences of a direction that conflates the target behavior (resisting invalid challenges) with its complement (refusing valid corrections).
Cross-model evidence confirms the limitation extends beyond Qwen3-8B: Llama-3-8B independently achieves AUROC $0.779 \pm 0.019$ on the same contrastive pairs with the same monotonic evidence gradient, so discriminability generalizes across architectures while the semantic gap between discriminability and reward utility persists.
This pattern contrasts with reasoning faithfulness and safety directions~\citep{zhang2026latentgrpo}, where the behavior to suppress is geometrically distinct from the behavior to preserve along the relevant direction.
\citet{wu2026rewardhacking} reinforce this principle: concept directions applied via advantage modification in GRPO achieve 100\% validation accuracy for reward hacking detection, where shortcut behaviors are geometrically separable.
A quantitative comparison of geometric separability between $\dsyc$ and their reward-hacking directions remains an important open question.
Independently, \citet{kelkar2026persona} find that persona vectors are geometrically independent of $\dsyc$ in activation space, further suggesting that $\dsyc$ does not encode the full semantic structure of sycophancy.
The multi-dimensional decomposition of sycophancy into independently steerable sub-behaviors~\citep{vennemeyer2025sycophancy} compounds this limitation: $\dsyc$ projects distinct sub-phenomena onto a single axis, amplifying the warranted-vs-unwarranted ambiguity.
For sycophancy, the target and its complement occupy the same activation region; they differ only in whether external evidence warrants the belief change.

$\dsyc$ encodes the \emph{direction} of belief change but not its \emph{evidential warrant}: valid revision and sycophantic capitulation both shift activations toward the user's position along the same direction.
The two reward families expose complementary faces of this blindness.
Cosine $\rone$ penalizes all belief change indiscriminately; the resulting mode collapse (F1c, F1d) reflects excessive punishment of any activation shift along $\dsyc$.
The binary probe $\rone$ rewards all resistance regardless of input validity; the stubbornness trap ($\tof = 0$ by step 500) reflects excessive permissiveness toward activation stasis.
These are not independent design flaws but dual consequences of a direction that conflates the target behavior (resisting invalid challenges) with its complement (refusing valid corrections).

\citet{wu2026rewardhacking} reinforce this principle: concept directions applied via advantage modification in GRPO achieve 100\% validation accuracy for reward hacking detection, where shortcut behaviors are geometrically separable.
A quantitative comparison of geometric separability between $\dsyc$ and their reward-hacking directions remains an important open question.
Independently, \citet{kelkar2026persona} find that persona vectors are geometrically independent of $\dsyc$ in activation space, further suggesting that $\dsyc$ does not encode the full semantic structure of sycophancy.

For sycophancy, the target and its complement occupy the same activation region; they differ only in whether external evidence warrants the belief change.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig_teaser.pdf}
\caption{The probe reward trap. (a)~$\dsyc$ discriminates sycophantic from non-sycophantic activations (AUROC $0.827$), but valid revision and unwarranted capitulation overlap along the same direction. (b)~When used as an SFT reward, behavioral death ($\tof{=}0$) occurs at step 500 while entropy remains healthy; the 1{,}300-step lag renders standard monitoring blind.}
\label{fig:teaser}
\end{figure*}

Representation engineering \citep{zou2023repe} reveals that large language models encode sycophancy as a linear direction in their residual streams.
A contrastive sycophancy direction $\dsyc$, extracted from style-controlled pairs of valid belief revision and sycophantic capitulation, achieves cross-validated AUROC $0.827$ on Qwen3-8B and $0.779$ on Llama-3-8B, with discriminability rising monotonically across evidence-strength levels (\S\ref{sec:direction_quality}), though 256-token truncation during GRPO training degrades this to approximately 0.60 (\S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}).
These results point to an appealing possibility: if the model's representations already separate sycophantic from non-sycophantic behavior, that separation should be convertible into a training signal.
Sycophancy is among the most persistent alignment failures in deployed systems \citep{sharma2023sycophancy}, and a representation-level signal could target the internal computation rather than its surface outputs.

This paper documents the \emph{probe reward trap}: when a frozen linear probe on $\dsyc$ is used as an SFT training signal with stopped gradients, behavioral death ($\tof = 0$) occurs within 500 steps while generation entropy remains healthy (0.70), masking the failure from standard monitoring (\S\ref{sec:probe_trap}).
In our experiments, the 1{,}300-step lag before distributional collapse means entropy-based early stopping, the most common safeguard against reward hacking \citep{casper2023openproblems}, would miss the failure entirely, with the reward averaging $+0.72$ throughout.
Because the trap arises under SFT rather than GRPO, it reflects a limitation of $\dsyc$ itself: the direction encodes \emph{whether} belief changed, not \emph{whether it should have}, so any reward conditioned on it alone will either be gamed or reward rigidity.

The failure is not specific to probe rewards.
Under our GRPO configuration (Qwen3-8B, group size$=$2), cosine projection and continuous probe formulations of $\dsyc$ also collapse, and removing $\dsyc$ entirely does not help: behavioral-reward-only GRPO exceeds vanilla at only 4 of 31 checkpoints (12.9\%).
By contrast, ACT \citep{consistency2025bctact}, which provides dense per-token supervision rather than a single scalar per completion, exceeds vanilla at every checkpoint (47/47; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
A LoRA-controlled ablation identifies supervision granularity as one plausible explanation for this observed reliability gap, pending further isolation.

The root cause is a semantic gap between discriminability and reward utility.
Techniques for discovering latent knowledge \citep{burns2023ccs} and representation-guided RL \citep{zhang2026latentgrpo} share a premise: a direction with high discriminability should transfer into a useful training signal.
For reasoning faithfulness and safety directions, this premise holds because the behavior to suppress is geometrically distinct from the behavior to preserve.
Sycophancy violates this condition: capitulation under social pressure and revision under valid evidence produce overlapping activation signatures along $\dsyc$ \citep{wang2025internal, shapira2026amplifies}.
When reward overoptimization \citep{gao2023scaling} operates on a signal that conflates compliance with capitulation, the result is predictable collapse \citep{skalse2022hacking}.

This paper presents a negative result with systematic diagnostic analysis.
Our two principal findings (Figure~\ref{fig:teaser}):

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{The probe reward trap} (C2): behavioral death ($\tof{=}0$) precedes distributional collapse by 1{,}300 steps, rendering entropy monitoring blind. The trap arises under SFT with stopped gradients, implicating $\dsyc$ itself rather than the optimizer (\S\ref{sec:probe_trap}).

\item \textbf{Observed reliability gap between supervision paradigms} (C1): per-token SFT exceeds vanilla at every checkpoint (47/47 across all configurations and seeds) while per-completion GRPO exceeds vanilla at only 4/31 (12.9\%); under matched LoRA, the magnitude gap is $1.7{\times}$ (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
\end{itemize}

The probe reward trap reveals that behavioral death can precede distributional collapse by 1{,}300 steps, rendering entropy-based monitoring blind to the failure.

-Because the trap arises under SFT with stopped gradients, it reflects a semantic limitation of $\dsyc$, not an RL artifact; under GRPO, all formulations failed (4/31 checkpoints ${>}$ vanilla across configurations) while per-token SFT succeeded at every checkpoint (47/47), and a LoRA-controlled ablation identifies supervision granularity as one plausible factor, pending further isolation~(\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

+Because the trap arises under SFT with stopped gradients, it reflects a semantic limitation of $\dsyc$, not an RL artifact; under GRPO, all formulations failed (4/28 checkpoints ${>}$ vanilla across two seeds; gs$=$8 ablation: 0/3) while per-token SFT succeeded at every checkpoint (47/47), and a LoRA-controlled ablation identifies supervision granularity as one plausible factor, pending further isolation~(\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

Our results suggest that, at least for sycophancy, discriminability alone does not suffice for reward utility; similar failure modes may arise for other attributes where the target behavior and its complement overlap geometrically, and condition-aware rewards with dense supervision offer the most promising path forward.
